Stated Claim / Post Context:
Basic income scheme protects rainforest, Belgium’s plant-based paradise, saving Patagonia’s biggest birds

In today's edition: a basic income pilot scheme sees 90% of participants in the Peruvian Amazon adopt environmentally friendly practices, the Belgian city of Ghent hits the Flemish government's green protein target, and a women-led team is bringing back rheas to Chilean Patagonia.

Actual Article Body:
Elizabeth Jacyshyn-Owen | Posted on October 21, 2026 |

Photo: Kjell Eson/Flickr (CC BY-NC-ND 2.0)

In today’s edition: a basic income pilot scheme sees 90% of participants in the Peruvian Amazon adopt environmentally friendly practices, the Belgian city of Ghent hits the Flemish government’s green protein target, and a women-led team is bringing back rheas to Chilean Patagonia.

A two-year pilot managed by the UK-based charity Cool Earth gave 211 people in three communities in Peru’s Asháninka region six cash transfers of 1,032 Peruvian soles each to spend as they wished. Researchers found almost 90% of participants adopted environmentally beneficial practices, such as collective reforestation, restoration of critical water sources and reductions of forest burning.

Source: The Guardian

In 2014, 13% of the population of this Belgian city described themselves as flexitarian. This year, 83% did. In 2021, the Flemish government launched the Green Deal Protein Shift – a commitment to switch the ratio of animal to plant proteins consumed from 60:40 to 40:60 by 2030. Ghent has already reached the target.

Source: The Guardian

The bill – which initially only proposed banning social media for those under the age of 16 – mandates strict verification and safeguards for personal data, as well as measures to tackle harmful and addictive platform features. Emails, private messaging apps and online gaming services intended for gameplay rather than social networking are not subject to restrictions.

Source: Daily Tribune

Daraxonrasib has already received FDA approval in the USA, and is recommended for adults with pancreatic cancer that has already spread to other organs and who have previously received at least one other treatment.

Source: Reuters

The 3.75 megawatt-hour lithium-ion battery system in a Buffalo, New York, apartment building is able to store excess energy generated and power the building when the grid is under pressure. The battery system can power the Peace Bridge Place affordable housing complex for several days at a time, and is one of the largest battery systems in a US residential building.

Source: AP News

Cooling systems are among the biggest energy users in food retail, and retailers are facing growing pressure to reduce energy consumption and emissions. At a supermarket in the German city of Darmstadt, a startup is testing a system that cools without traditional refrigerants, using magnets, water and special metal alloys instead.

Source: Deutsche Welle

The city-funded programme aims to avoid pet owners surrendering their animals to shelters by offering free pet food at 22 pantries across all five boroughs. The Campaign Against Hunger already gives pet food to clients, but obtaining those supplies can be challenging and often requires seeking grants and support from foundations and donors.

Source: ABC7NY

More than 1,200 volunteers have come together to create woodland over an equivalent area of 154 football pitches, comprised of 61 new orchards and 17 micro-forests. During the past two tree-planting seasons, the Lancashire Woodland Partnership has also planted roughly half a million trees and over 27,000 metres of new hedges.

Source: BBC News

The TRANSITional Art Project includes murals and photography from New Jersey-based artists featured in temporary visual art exhibitions at NJ Transit bus and train stations across the State.

Source: WHYY

Along with Tompkins Conservation and the Rewilding Chile Foundation, a team of female rangers acquired former ranchlands and began removing thousands of kilometres of fencing, letting native wildlife reclaim the landscape.

Source: Mongabay
